w: This Roman Catholic church carries two names - Notre-Dame-de-l'Immaculee-Conception and, older still, Notre-Dame-de-la-Platea - a double christening that hints at centuries of rebuilding on the same site above the old port. It is protected today as a listed historic monument on the French Riviera.
s: A cathedral with two names above the old port
_facts: Known by two French names: Notre-Dame-de-l'Immaculee-Conception and Notre-Dame-de-la-Platea
Listed and protected as a historic monument

w: Before it was the Hotel du Cap-Eden-Roc, this Cap d'Antibes landmark opened in 1870 as a private mansion called Villa Soleil. It turned hotel in 1889, and has been drawing the Riviera's summer crowd to its rocky point at the tip of the cape ever since.
s: A private mansion turned Riviera hotel, 1889
_facts: Opened 1870 as a private mansion, Villa Soleil

n: Jardin botanique de la Villa Thuret
w: Laid out across 3.5 hectares on the grounds of the Villa Thuret in Antibes Juan-les-Pins, this botanical garden has long served as a trial ground for species suited to the Riviera's mild climate. It costs nothing to walk its paths on weekdays - one of the coast's quieter free pleasures.
s: 3.5 free hectares of exotic trees by the sea
_facts: 3.5-hectare botanical garden on the grounds of the Villa Thuret

w: Also known as the Manoir de Vaugrenier, this mansion in nearby Villeneuve-Loubet was raised across the 17th and 18th centuries. The French Ministry of Culture listed it as a historic monument in 1992, a quiet counterpoint to Antibes' better-known ramparts just down the coast.
_facts: Also called the Manoir de Vaugrenier
Listed as a historic monument by the French Ministry of Culture since 1992

w: On the Garoupe plateau above Cap d'Antibes, this church is unusual for its double nave, each with its own Madonna: Notre-Dame de la Garde on the right, Notre-Dame de Bon Port on the left. Bon Port is patron saint of Antibes' sailors, honoured each July with a procession carrying her statue through town.
s: Two naves, two Madonnas, one sailors' saint
_facts: Sits on the Garoupe plateau overlooking Cap d'Antibes
Has two naves, each with its own Madonna statue
Notre-Dame de Bon Port is patron saint of Antibes' sailors
Annual July procession carries her statue through town

w: American architect Barry Dierks built this Modernist villa in 1938 for Palm Beach socialite Audrey Chadwick, one of the most distinctive of his Riviera commissions. Raised on the eve of the Second World War, it stands as one of the last Modernist houses built on this coast before the style fell silent for years.
s: The Riviera's last Modernist villa before the war
_facts: Built for Palm Beach socialite Audrey Chadwick
One of the last Modernist buildings raised on the Riviera before WWII
